$comment: Canonical Anthropic Messages API tool definitions for the Clinical Co-Pilot -- the contract, not the implementation (PUNCH_LIST_2.md Item 4). ChartContextTools::definitions() and CopilotService::submitAnswerToolDefinition() load from this file via ToolSchemaRegistry rather than hand-rewriting it inline. Field names (name, description, input_schema) match Anthropic's wire format exactly -- see vendor/anthropic-ai/sdk/src/Beta/Messages/BetaTool.php's #[Required('input_schema')] attribute; a prior inline copy of these definitions used camelCase 'inputSchema' for the four chart tools, which Anthropic's API does not recognize (silently harmless only because all four take no arguments to begin with). An empty 'properties: {}' here is loaded and re-encoded as a PHP stdClass by ToolSchemaRegistry, not a plain array -- confirmed against the real API, which rejects an empty properties re-serialized as a JSON array ('Input should be an object') the way a naive json_decode(..., associative: true) round-trip would produce.

tools.name: get_a1c_series
tools.description: Hemoglobin A1c results for this patient over time, oldest first, with value, units, reference range and abnormal flag. Use for questions about glycaemic control, diabetes trajectory, or whether the patient is improving.

tools.name: get_active_problems
tools.description: The active problem list for this patient: title, coded diagnosis, onset date and outcome. Use to establish what conditions the patient carries.

tools.name: get_medications
tools.description: Currently active prescriptions: drug, dosage, form, interval, route and start date. Use for questions about treatment, adherence or therapy changes.

tools.name: get_recent_encounters
tools.description: The most recent encounters for this patient: date, reason and encounter type. Use to establish recent clinical activity or visit history.

tools.name: get_extracted_documents
tools.description: Structured data previously extracted from documents (lab PDFs and intake forms) the physician has uploaded and attached to this patient's chart via the Clinical Co-Pilot, most recent first -- document type, when it was extracted, and the extracted fields as JSON. Use for questions about an uploaded lab report, intake form, or any other attached document.

tools.name: search_guideline_evidence
tools.description: Hybrid (keyword + semantic) search over a small clinical-guideline reference corpus (FDA drug-label sections: contraindications, warnings, drug interactions, dosing), reranked for relevance. Returns the top matching evidence chunks with source metadata. Use for questions about a medication's safety profile, interactions, contraindications or dosing guidance -- not for anything specific to this patient's own chart.

query.description: What to search for, e.g. a drug name plus the safety question ("metformin contraindications renal impairment").

tools.name: consult_chart_worker
tools.description: Consult the chart-data specialist: returns four structured data sources for this patient in one bundled response, keyed by name -- get_a1c_series, get_active_problems, get_medications, get_recent_encounters. Use for questions about diagnoses, treatment, glycaemic control, or visit history. When citing a claim via submit_answer, its citation.source_id must be the specific data-source key inside the bundle (e.g. get_medications), not consult_chart_worker itself.

tools.name: consult_document_worker
tools.description: Consult the document-data specialist: returns data previously extracted from documents (lab PDFs and intake forms) the physician has uploaded and attached to this patient's chart, keyed as get_extracted_documents. Use for questions about an uploaded lab report, intake form, or any other attached document. When citing a claim via submit_answer, its citation.source_id must be get_extracted_documents, not consult_document_worker itself.

tools.name: consult_evidence_worker
tools.description: Consult the guideline-evidence specialist: runs a hybrid search over a small clinical-guideline corpus for the given query and returns the top matching evidence chunks, keyed as search_guideline_evidence. Use for questions about a medication's safety profile, interactions, contraindications or dosing guidance. When citing a claim via submit_answer, its citation.source_id must be search_guideline_evidence, not consult_evidence_worker itself.

query.description: What to search for, e.g. a drug name plus the safety question.

tools.name: submit_answer
tools.description: Give your final answer to the clinician. Every clinical claim must carry a citation object grounding it in a tool call made this turn. citation.source_type is one of chart_tool (structured OpenEMR data), lab_pdf or intake_form (document extraction), or guideline (guideline evidence). citation.source_id is always the specific tool call that supports the claim (e.g. get_medications, get_extracted_documents, search_guideline_evidence) -- never a worker's name (consult_chart_worker/consult_document_worker/consult_evidence_worker are not valid citations). citation.quote_or_value is the exact value or quote grounding the claim. citation.field_or_chunk_id is required for EVERY source_type, chart_tool included: for a chart_tool citation it is the name of the field in the tool's row that you are quoting (e.g. title or diagnosis for get_active_problems, drug or dosage for get_medications, value or result_date for get_a1c_series, reason for get_recent_encounters); for a guideline citation it is the chunk_id. citation.page_or_section is required for every source_type except chart_tool, where a database row has no page. For lab_pdf and intake_form citations, also copy citation.document_id and citation.bbox verbatim from the extracted document's fields.source_citation (returned by get_extracted_documents) -- never invent either; if the extracted document has none, omit both rather than guessing. If the tool results do not contain enough information to answer the question, set insufficient_information to true instead of guessing.

insufficient_information.description: True if the tool results do not contain enough information to answer the question.

summary.description: Optional framing text with no clinical claims of its own (e.g. "Based on the chart:"), or the full honest answer when insufficient_information is true.

claims.description: One entry per clinical claim in the answer. Omit or leave empty when insufficient_information is true.

citation.description: Where this claim's grounding came from.

source_id.description: The specific tool call made this turn that supports this claim, e.g. get_medications.

page_or_section.description: Page or section within the source. Not applicable for chart_tool citations.

field_or_chunk_id.description: Required for every source_type, including chart_tool. The specific field or chunk within the source: the name of the row field you are quoting (e.g. drug, value, title) or a retrieval chunk id.

quote_or_value.description: The exact quoted text or value grounding this claim.

document_id.description: Required for lab_pdf/intake_form citations: the document_id copied verbatim from that document's fields.source_citation. Never invent this value.

bbox.description: Required for lab_pdf/intake_form citations: the bounding box copied verbatim from that document's fields.source_citation.bbox.

x0.description: Left edge, normalized 0.0-1.0 against page width.

y0.description: Top edge, normalized 0.0-1.0 against page height.

x1.description: Right edge, normalized 0.0-1.0 against page width.

y1.description: Bottom edge, normalized 0.0-1.0 against page height.
